assumptions.probe_density_reason: Nominal steel density; exact probe mass is not measured. Report actual path tracking separately.
assumptions.xy_inertia: symmetric uniform prism approximation from published polar inertia and thickness
assumptions.support: flat plane, gravity along -z; sparse mesh-plane contacts do not establish uniform pressure
assumptions.contact: MuJoCo solref=[0.001, 1], solimp=[0.99, 0.99, 0.001], elliptic cone, 0.5 ms timestep
assumptions.probe_drive: Dynamic x/y translation joints keep probe vertical at declared height; welded to prescribed mocap target with solref=[0.001, 1], solimp=[0.99, 0.99, 0.001]. Actual probe tracking is checked.

evidence_limits: The hex trajectory has been inspected during development and is no longer held-out evidence.
No synchronized camera footage; visual reconstruction is unvalidated.
Geometry is compared with the author's published specification, not a new independent measurement.
Force measurements are retained in the source but not compared by this example.
Recording ends with the push; no measured static settling interval is declared.
Support pressure distribution and exact contact compliance are not measured.
reuse: No dataset-wide reuse license was found in the source repository. Downloaded raw data remains local under runs/ and is not bundled. See original authors for reuse terms.
citation: Kuan-Ting Yu, Maria Bauza, Nima Fazeli, Alberto Rodriguez. More than a Million Ways to Be Pushed: A High-Fidelity Experimental Dataset of Planar Pushing. IROS 2016. https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.04038

probe.source: Paper section IV-A and pinned collectors: default probe5, contact height calculation. Friction is the approximate measured probe/object value, not a per-trial measurement.
